title: Macros
goal: Record an edit once and replay it on dozens of lines, reliably.

lessons.title: Recording and replaying

concepts.desc: record every key you press into register a, until q.
replay register a.
replay the macro you ran last.
replay 5 times. It stops early if any step fails.
repeat the last command-line command.

lessons.tip: Before recording, picture the edit as it would work on ANY line, not just this one. Finish the macro on the next line (j) so you can chain it.

quiz.q: Start recording a macro into register q.
quiz.a: qq

quiz.q: Run macro q 20 times.
Re-run the macro you just ran.
How do you stop recording?
quiz.a: Press q (in normal mode).

quiz.q: Why do macros usually end with j?
quiz.a: So the cursor is on the next line, ready for the next run.

quiz.q: What happens to the rest of 50@a if a motion fails on run 12?
quiz.a: The macro stops; the remaining runs are skipped.

lessons.title: Robust macros

concepts.desc: start with a known position on the line, not wherever the cursor happened to be.
move with motions that work whatever the text length; avoid l counts.
start with a search so the macro finds its own next target.
with a huge count, the macro runs until it fails, e.g. j on the last line.
make searches fail at the end of the file so search macros don't loop forever.

lessons.tip: Test a new macro on one line (@a), check it, then run it with a count. If it went wrong, u undoes the whole run.

quiz.q: Why start a line macro with 0 or ^?
quiz.a: So it works the same wherever the cursor was on the line.

quiz.q: Your macro uses `5l` to reach the second field. Why is that fragile, and what's better?
quiz.a: Field widths vary; use f, / W / t motions instead.

quiz.q: How can a macro that only edits matching lines find the next one?
quiz.a: Start (or end) it with a search: /pattern<CR> or n.

quiz.q: You run 999@a with a search macro and it never stops. Why?
quiz.a: The search wraps around to the top (wrapscan); :set nowrapscan stops it at the end.

quiz.q: Undo a whole macro run of 10 iterations.
quiz.a: u (once per @a/10@a command; one undo step per run).

quiz.q: Run a macro until it fails, without counting lines.
quiz.a: Use a big count, e.g. 999@a.

lessons.title: Recursive macros

concepts.desc: clear register a (record nothing), so the recursive call does nothing while recording.
a macro that calls itself at the end.
runs until a step fails (end of file, search not found).
the failing motion is what stops the recursion.

lessons.tip: Always clear the register first (qaq). Otherwise the old contents of a run during recording and make a mess.

quiz.q: Why type qaq before recording a recursive macro?
quiz.a: To empty register a so the @a inside the recording does nothing.

quiz.q: What stops a recursive macro?
quiz.a: A failing step, e.g. j/↓ on the last line or a search with no more matches.

quiz.q: Write the key sequence skeleton for a recursive macro in register b.
quiz.a: qbq qb ...edits... j@b q (↓@b also works), then @b

quiz.q: Advantage of a recursive macro over 100@a?
quiz.a: You don't have to guess a count; it naturally runs to the end.

quiz.q: During recording, does the @a at the end do anything?
quiz.a: No (the register is empty), it's just recorded.

quiz.q: A recursive search macro loops forever. Fix?
quiz.a: :set nowrapscan (so the search fails at the end of the file).

lessons.title: Editing macros and :normal

concepts.desc: write a macro directly as text.
paste a macro onto a line, fix it, yank it back (0"ay$).
append more keys to an existing macro by recording with the uppercase name.
run normal-mode keys on every line of a range, e.g. :%norm A;
run a macro on every selected line (press : in visual mode).
run it on every line matching pat (more in week 8).

lessons.tip: :norm runs from the start of each line and keeps going after a failing line, so it's often more forgiving than counts.

quiz.q: Append ; to every line in the file without a macro.
quiz.a: :%norm A;

quiz.q: Run macro a on lines 10 to 20.
quiz.a: :10,20norm @a

quiz.q: How do you fix a typo inside a recorded macro?
quiz.a: Paste it ("ap), edit the line, yank it back (0"ay$), then delete the line. Or :let @a='...'.

quiz.q: Add more steps to the end of macro a.
quiz.a: qA ... q (record with the uppercase register).

quiz.q: Run macro a on every selected line.
quiz.a: :'<,'>norm @a (press : in visual mode, then norm @a)

quiz.q: Run a macro only on lines containing TODO.
quiz.a: :g/TODO/norm @a

lessons.title: Week 7 review

concepts.desc: record and replay
robust positioning
recursion
editing and ranges

lessons.tip: If you're about to do the same edit for the third time, stop and record it.

quiz.q: Record a macro in w that appends a comma and moves down.
quiz.a: qwA,<Esc>jq

quiz.q: Run macro w on every line of the current paragraph.
quiz.a: vip:norm @w

quiz.q: Inspect what's in macro w.
quiz.a: :reg w

quiz.q: Repeat the last :command.
Make a macro that finds and processes each line with FIXME, to the end of the file only.
quiz.a: :set nowrapscan, then qa/FIXME<CR>...q and 999@a (or a recursive macro)

quiz.q: Why can't you use 5l to move to a CSV's second field in a macro?
quiz.a: The first field's length varies per line; use f, instead.
